title: Fix the HashSet That Allows Duplicates
description: The program should store Point objects in a HashSet, treating two points with the same coordinates as duplicates.
expectedBehavior: The program should print 1, since both points represent the same coordinates.
actualProblem: Point never overrides equals() and hashCode(), so HashSet falls back to the default identity-based comparison — each new Point(1, 2) is a distinct object, so both are added and size() prints 2 instead of 1.
explanation: HashSet relies on equals() and hashCode() to detect duplicates. Without overriding both consistently, two objects with identical data are still treated as different because they're different objects in memory.
